facts.value: By October 28, 2026, the Spectator reported that Lowndes County's 60-day moratorium on applications to build AI data centers had ended.
facts.supporting_summary: The local news article explicitly describes the moratorium as ended; it does not give an exact expiration date.

facts.value: At its October 27, 2026 regular meeting, the Lowndes County Board of Commissioners announced a planned November 2 release of a data-center ordinance draft.
facts.supporting_summary: The article reports the announcement and scheduled release, rather than confirming that the release occurred.

facts.value: A Lowndes County Data Center Ordinance draft is dated November 2, 2026 and proposes Chapter 7 of the Unified Land Development Code.
facts.supporting_summary: The supplied document identifies itself as a draft and gives its proposed chapter and date.

facts.value: The November 2, 2026 draft synopsis describes proposed requirements for data-center development, construction, operation and decommissioning in unincorporated Lowndes County.
facts.supporting_summary: The synopsis says the proposed ordinance would apply, once approved, to new data centers and operational expansions after adoption.

facts.value: The draft synopsis would allow principal-use data centers in industrial districts subject to supplemental standards and would require a favorable commissioners' decision before permit applications.
facts.supporting_summary: The listed proposed standards cover site and building characteristics, environmental and utility issues, and fire suppression. The procedure refers to a public hearing and a preponderance-of-the-evidence standard.

facts.value: The commissioners were scheduled to accept resident feedback on the draft at their November 10, 2026 meeting.
facts.supporting_summary: The October 28 article presents feedback as a future event, not a completed action.

facts.value: The commissioners were scheduled to vote for or against the data-center ordinance on December 8, 2026.
facts.supporting_summary: The article describes a planned vote and does not establish its outcome.

facts.value: Residents first learned of plans for an AI data center in July 2025, after land near the Foxborough subdivision was rezoned for light industrial use.
facts.locator: Paragraph on residents discovering the plans
facts.supporting_summary: The article associates discovery of the plans with the earlier rezoning.

facts.value: Lowndes Citizens Against Data Centers has opposed data centers since December 2025, according to the October 28, 2026 article.
facts.supporting_summary: The article identifies LCAD as a local activist group and dates the start of its opposition.

facts.value: The supplied archive index lists commission agendas and minutes through December 9, 2025, but captures no 2026 commission minutes.
facts.locator: Commission Meeting Agendas and Commission Meeting Minutes sections
facts.supporting_summary: This is an observation about the supplied index, not evidence that no later meeting or legal action occurred.
